reasons.plausibility: The hypothesis is scientifically sound: V is a known grain-boundary strengthener in steels and could form ductile precipitates, but the specific claim that 2 wt% V will form grain-boundary precipitates in this complex high-entropy alloy without altering the caloric matrix is speculative and lacks direct supporting evidence for this system.
reasons.testability: The proposed test is clear and decisive: it specifies a control group, microstructural characterization (TEM), and quantitative pass/fail criteria (≥30% strength increase, <5% caloric change), which would directly falsify the hypothesis if not met.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis is highly useful as it proposes a novel, rare-earth-free alloying strategy to simultaneously improve mechanical integrity and preserve caloric performance, directly addressing the core limitation of the material.
